# Dependencies

```{r}

library(dplyr) # for %>%, mutate, filter, count, summarize, group_by, coalesce
library(tidyr) # for pivot_longer, pivot_wider, separate
library(tibble) # for tribble
library(stringr) # for str_ functions
library(forcats) # for fct
library(ggplot2) # for ggplot

```

# Today's data

`dat_wellbeing_wide`: one row per participant, with wellbeing scores at three timepoints in separate columns. Participant 4 did not complete the follow-up.

`dat_items`: one row per participant, with responses to three items from a depression scale (PHQ) and three items from an anxiety scale (GAD), each scored 0 to 3.

`dat_sessions`: one row per session, with the date each session was completed.

`dat_versions`: age was saved in a different column in each of three versions of a survey.

`dat_meta_wide`: summary statistics from three studies, one row per study.

```{r}

dat_wellbeing_wide <- tribble(
  ~id, ~condition,     ~wellbeing_baseline, ~wellbeing_post, ~wellbeing_followup,
  1,   "control",      12,                  13,              12,
  2,   "intervention", 11,                  16,              15,
  3,   "waitlist",     13,                  13,              14,
  4,   "control",      14,                  14,              NA,
  5,   "intervention", 10,                  15,              14,
  6,   "waitlist",     12,                  12,              13
)

dat_items <- tribble(
  ~id, ~phq_1, ~phq_2, ~phq_3, ~gad_1, ~gad_2, ~gad_3,
  1,   0,      1,      0,      1,      1,      0,
  2,   2,      3,      2,      3,      2,      2,
  3,   1,      1,      2,      1,      NA,     1,
  4,   3,      2,      3,      2,      3,      3,
  5,   0,      0,      1,      0,      1,      0,
  6,   1,      2,      1,      2,      1,      2
)

dat_sessions <- tribble(
  ~id, ~timepoint,  ~wellbeing, ~date,
  1,   "baseline",  12,         "2024-03-01",
  1,   "post",      13,         "2024-03-15",
  2,   "baseline",  11,         "2024-03-02",
  2,   "post",      16,         "2024-03-16",
  3,   "baseline",  13,         "2024-03-02",
  3,   "post",      13,         "2024-03-17",
  3,   "post",      14,         "2024-03-18"
)

dat_versions <- tribble(
  ~id, ~age_v1, ~age_v2, ~age_v3,
  1,   23,      NA,      NA,
  2,   NA,      31,      NA,
  3,   NA,      NA,      27,
  4,   45,      NA,      46,
  5,   NA,      NA,      NA
)

dat_meta_wide <- tribble(
  ~study,       ~mean_trt, ~sd_trt, ~n_trt, ~mean_ctrl, ~sd_ctrl, ~n_ctrl,
  "Smith 2019", 12.1,      4.2,     30,     15.3,       4.8,      31,
  "Jones 2021", 8.4,       3.1,     52,     9.9,        3.5,      50,
  "Lee 2022",   20.5,      6.0,     18,     24.1,       6.4,      20
)

```

# Tidy data

## Which rule is broken?

The same wellbeing data was also exported in the format below. Which rule of Tidy Data does it break? Use `separate()` to fix it, so that 'baseline' and 'post' are numeric columns.

```{r}

dat_wellbeing_messy <- tribble(
  ~id, ~baseline_post,
  1,   "12/13",
  2,   "11/16",
  3,   "13/13"
)

```

# `pivot_longer()`

## Wide to long

Pivot `dat_wellbeing_wide` to long format, with one row per participant per timepoint and columns 'timepoint' and 'wellbeing'. Specify the `cols` argument in three different ways: with `starts_with()`, with negative selection, and with a range of columns using `:`.

```{r}



```

## Predict before you run

Before running: what will happen? Why?

```{r}
#| error: true

dat_wellbeing_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -id,
               names_to = "timepoint",
               values_to = "wellbeing")

```

Then convert 'timepoint' to a factor in a meaningful order, calculate the mean wellbeing in each condition at each timepoint, and save the long data as `dat_wellbeing_long`.

# Fix the broken pipe

This code is meant to calculate the mean change in wellbeing from baseline to post in each condition. It has (at least) four bugs. Find and fix them one at a time.

```{r}
#| eval: false

dat_wellbeing_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -id,
               names_to = "timepoint",
               values_to = "wellbeing",
               names_prefix = "wellbeing") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = wellbeing,
              values_from = timepoint) %>%
  mutate(change = post - baseline) %>%
  summarize(mean_change = mean(change))

```

Imagine that the participants' age and gender were stored in a separate data frame, `dat_demographics`, with one row per participant and an 'id' column. How would you add them to `dat_scale_scores`? Why would putting the two data frames side by side not be a safe way to do this?
